notes.title: 🔥 Dynamic Fire System – Dev Showcase | The Old War 🔥
notes.notes:
[p][dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pa07dJ1NgR8"][/dynamiclink][b]Dev Update: Fire System in The Old War[/b][/p][p]
Hey everyone! Just wanted to share a behind-the-scenes look at one of the new features we’ve been working on - a[b] fully dynamic fire simulation system[/b] that brings more chaos, strategy, and atmosphere to [i]The Old War[/i].[/p][p][b]So what does it do?[/b]
Our fire system isn't just for show. Here's what makes it unique:[/p][list][*][p][b]Fires grow, spread, and consume fuel[/b] realistically over time. A small spark can turn into a devastating inferno, or fizzle out if it runs out of fuel.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Fire size, heat, and spread radius[/b] dynamically increase and shrink based on available fuel and surrounding conditions.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Visual effects scale with the fire's intensity[/b], so you’ll [i]see[/i] small flickers turn into raging blazes.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Weather, wind, and snow[/b] can influence the spread rate and visual behavior.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Thousands of fire instances[/b] can exist on-screen simultaneously, thanks to an efficient ECS-based architecture (DOTS) + GPU-driven VFX Graph integration.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Buildings char and darken[/b] over time as they burn, with a visual charring system that reflects how much fuel remains.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Why it matters:[/b]
Fires in [i]The Old War[/i] aren’t just eye candy - they’re tactical. You might burn down an enemy’s key structure… but what if the fire spreads to a neutral city? Or worse, your own base? Fire is now a [b]strategic weapon[/b], but it comes with risks.[/p][p]🛠️ [b]Tech side for the curious:[/b][/p][list][*][p]We're using Unity's Entity Component System (ECS) and VFX Graph to manage massive numbers of fires without tanking performance.[/p][/*][*][p]Fires are data-driven, so they can interact with other systems like weather, capture mechanics, and faction AI.[/p][/*][*][p]We're also experimenting with a [b]visual effect pooling system[/b] and tight AABB bounds to ensure only visible VFX are simulated.[/p][/*][/list][p]Here's a sneak peek of what it looks like in action:[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p] [b]Wishlist The Old War on Steam:[/b] 
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1248750/The_Old_War/"][/dynamiclink] [/p][p] [b]Join the Community on Discord: [url="https://discord.gg/Dw2u7gQ8UV"]https://discord.gg/Dw2u7gQ8UV[/url][/b] [/p][p] [b]Learn more: [url="http://warcheststudios.com/"]http://warcheststudios.com/[/url][/b][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]💬 Let us know what you think!
Would you ever risk setting a blaze near your own walls? Want us to add fire-based traps or firefighting units? We’d love your feedback as we refine the system.[/p][p]Stay warm out there,
—Dan
[i]Warchest Studios[/i][/p]

notes.title: MASSIVE BATTLES UNLOCKED!
notes.notes:
[p][b]MASSIVE BATTLES UNLOCKED![/b][dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MNDxuM1rqwQ"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]This is a really exciting post for me. The Old War can now support thousands of units at one time! [/p][p]As much as I love other games with massive swarms, there are many reasons I am excited for a high unit limit. We aren't looking to be a tower defense, or a swarm-centric game, but we don't want to limit you to a unit cap that has been outdated for 20 years. For The Old War, a high unit count is more about the additional gameplay mechanics and new strategies that this unlocks.[/p][p][/p][p]Some of this new, emergent gameplay is as follows and will be explained further:[/p][list][*][p]Neutral Towns and Cities[/p][/*][*][p]Swarm-type Troops[/p][/*][*][p]Shared Unit Control at Scale[/p][/*][*][p]A Living, Breathing World[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]NEUTRAL CITIES AND TOWNS[/b][/p][list][*][p]Adds [i]territorial strategy[/i] - towns can be occupied, allied with, razed, or fortified.[/p][/*][*][p]Forces players to consider diplomacy or resource denial, not just combat. People can be a resource for a number of nefarious purposes - recruits, labour, or just bodies for the undead.[/p][/*][*][p]Offers a strategic midpoint between battles, capture a town to resupply or reinforce before a major siege. Each battle will be a series of skirmishes and escalating conflicts.[/p][/*][*][p]You may need to protect allied cities, or wipe them out to prevent their exploitation by others.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][b]SWARM TROOPS[/b][/p][list][*][p]Enables [i]quantity-over-quality[/i] factions or tactics, throw waves of weak units to overwhelm, scout, or soak damage.[/p][/*][*][p]Introduces [i]attrition mechanics[/i] - can you outlast the swarm? Can you keep producing faster than they die?[/p][/*][*][p]Opens up asymmetrical strategies: fighting a swarm requires choke points, AoE attacks, or elite squads.[/p][/*][*][p]Adds chaos and urgency - when 300 units are charging your gate, every second matters.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]SHARED UNIT CONTROL AT SCALE[/b][/p][list][*][p]Enables [i]true co-op strategy[/i], where one player can manage the frontlines, another handles ranged units, another controls cavalry or siege weapons. It will be a struggle for one commander to control it all.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduces micromanagement stress, allowing teams to act like a real military command structure.[/p][/*][*][p]Lets players [i]specialize[/i] based on preference - some love building bases, others love commanding troops.[/p][/*][*][p]Keeps large-scale battles manageable and exciting, not overwhelming.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]A LIVING, BREATHING, WORLD[/b][/p][list][*][p]The world reacts: citizens flee if you are a conqueror, towns change hands, citizens remember past battles.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Roaming Beasts[/b]: Neutral creatures roam the map: wolves, bears, magical entities. Can be hunted, avoided, or even tamed.[/p][/*][*][p]Trade routes move between towns. Can be intercepted or protected, affecting economies.
[/p][/*][/list][p]Thousands of units don’t just make the battles bigger - they make the choices deeper. Every formation, every frontline, every village caught in the crossfire becomes part of The Old War. This is war at a scale where your strategy is shaped by the world itself.[/p][p][/p][p]Wishlist [i]The Old War[/i] on Steam:[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1248750/The_Old_War/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: The Clan System
notes.notes: [h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/e0a149a14046efd6c99a4518ab60ea54af218ffa.png"][/img][/h3][h3]Introducing Clans in [i]The Old War[/i] - Build Together, Fight Together[/h3][p]The battlefield is brutal, but you don’t have to face it alone.[/p][p]With the new [b]Clan System[/b], you and your friends can forge a shared legacy. Whether you're building a warband of elite fighters or managing a growing municipal workforce, clans let you combine your efforts and push back the darkness together.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][b]Shared Armies & Resources[/b][/p][p]When you form a clan, all members contribute to a [b]shared pool of units, resources, and structures[/b]. This isn’t just a stat screen, these are real assets that persist between battles. What you build or lose affects the entire clan, so strategy and coordination matter.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][b]Assign Player Roles[/b][/p][p]Every clan can assign [b]Council Seats[/b], each with their own unique roles and benefits. [/p][p]These roles include:[/p][list][*][p]Warlord[/p][/*][*][p]Grand Mage[/p][/*][*][p]Questor[/p][/*][*][p]Alderman[/p][/*][*][p]Quartermaster[/p][/*][/list][p]Whether you're leading attacks or handling supply chains, everyone has a part to play. Roles aren't just cosmetic, they shape how your faction functions.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][b]Commit to Battles as a Clan[/b][/p][p]Before entering a battle, the clan can [b]draw from its shared forces[/b], choosing which units to risk and which to preserve. Committing to a fight is a real decision with long-term consequences. Lose a veteran unit, and it's gone for good unless your clan has the resources to rebuild.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][b]Customize Your Regalia[/b][/p][p]Clans can also design their own [b]banners, colors, and regalia[/b]. These symbols appear on your units, buildings, and UI, so when your army marches into battle, the enemy knows who’s coming.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]This system is built to support [b]cooperative, long-term strategy[/b]. It’s not just about winning a match, it’s about forging a legacy everyone will remember.[/p][p][/p][p]The Clan System is still evolving, and your feedback is hugely valuable. What kinds of roles, permissions, or visuals would [i]you[/i] like to see added?[/p]

notes.title: Let There Be Magic!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/b578bc3d822dd197a4374b3e3aae0cf75388e86b.png[/img][h2]Magic in The Old War[/h2]

In The Old War, magic is hated and feared. 

It was said that magic is what destroyed the world. Anyone who uses it plays with forces far beyond their comprehension and control. Only tyrants and madmen would dabble in these forces.

[h2]How it Affects the Game[/h2]
This plays a major factor on the battlefields of the Old War. Magic is wildly powerful and unpredictable.

The world is unstable. Every spell cast rocks the stability of the world, and can cause unprecedented devastation. If you cast a spell, instability increases, the day/night cycle speeds up, and random cataclysmic events will start to happen. Tornados, firestorms, lightning, portals to other dimensions, and more.

Here is just a taste of what is to come.

[previewyoutube=4Yr7t11mGg0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]What's Coming Next?[/h2]

Clearly, two spells is no problem for even a junior wizard to master. More spells and disciplines can be mastered, greatly enhancing the specificity and destructive potential of each wizard.

Any spells or abilities that you think should be added? Portals? Ice storms? Elementals?

notes.title: The Old War – Persistent Armies
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/9979722e04290e7c4dee9a7c7a82413206b11435.png[/img]

[h1]Core Gameplay Mechanics at Launch[/h1]

Commanders, the time has come to prepare for The Old War. As the release draws near, we want to highlight the mechanics that will shape your experience in this dark and unforgiving world.

In The Old War, you’ll lead a persistent army—an embattled force that survives the ravages of war, grows stronger through experience, and faces the consequences of every battle fought.

[h2]The Value of Preserving Your Army[/h2]
Every unit counts in The Old War, and that includes your workers. Your workforce is divided into three tiers: Apprentice, Artisan, and Architect. Losing one of these highly skilled workers can have devastating consequences on your war effort, so preserving your army’s strength is critical to long-term success.

[h2]Unit Heroization[/h2]
Over time, individual units can become heroes. Through valor and experience, a unit can rise above the ranks and gain unique abilities, becoming a pivotal force in your ongoing campaigns.

[h2]Win the War, Even if You Lose a Battle[/h2]
In The Old War, you don’t simply fight for immediate victory. Your army persists between battles, and you may find yourself in battles where resource gathering is just as important as fighting. Your opponent may be focused on total annihilation, while you aim to build and gather strength for the war to come. Lost battles don’t necessarily mean a lost war—it’s all about adapting your strategy and resources for the long haul.

[previewyoutube=7y1bTAzXQbw;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Faction-Based Experience[/h2]
Your army grows stronger as you fight against specific enemies. For example, battling the undead will turn your forces into undead-killing machines, making your faction more effective against certain threats as you progress.

[h1]What’s Next?[/h1]
This is just the beginning. The Old War will continue to evolve with more units, mechanics, and expansive battles as we get closer to launch. Get ready for a dynamic, ever-changing RTS where no two battles are ever the same. 

If you are interested in shaping the future of The Old War, feel free to add a wishlist or drop a comment, I'd love to hear what you think about it!

notes.title: Kingdom of Andar Construction System
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/ddb05d6a7621cb31496759df22e1c05f1f22786d.png[/img]
Hello Everyone!

Today, we’re diving into the construction system for the main human faction in The Old War, The Kingdom of Andar. This post will cover everything from placement mechanics to dynamic destruction, giving you a clear understanding of how to plan, build, and maintain your settlements. 

Historically in strategy games, humans are the quintessential base builder with a familiar set of rules. This is why I've decided to start with a familiar faction. The Kingdom are not the only human faction, but they are the most familiar. They expand their territory using fortifications and roads to connect cities and trade routes, giving them places of refuge when the sun sets.

[h1]Placement Mechanics[/h1]
Building placement for Andarian architects in The Old War is influenced by several key factors:

[list]
[*] [b]Spheres of Influence[/b] – Buildings must be placed within the controlled area of your faction (more on this below).
[*] [b]Building Requirements[/b] – Certain structures need certain requirements to be built.
[*] [b]Obstruction Rules[/b] – You cannot place structures too close to enemy buildings, natural obstacles, or units.
[*] [b]Destruction System[/b] – While most buildings adhere to a loose grid for ease of placement, smaller structures have more flexibility.[/list]

[h2]Spheres of Influence[/h2]
The Kingdom of Andar expands their territory through a methodical, risk averse approach, with each move planned carefully to preserve human lives. Town Centers, Outposts, and Fortifications. Each structure projects a Sphere of Influence, allowing new buildings to be placed within its radius. If a structure falls outside this zone, construction will be blocked until influence is extended.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/eefb14d3e758fdb50266cc29325f43de525338be.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]Town Centers[/b] provide the largest influence radius.
[*] [b]Outposts[/b] serve as forward-expansion points, granting a smaller zone of control, but allowing construction outside of your zone of control.
[*] [b]Fortifications & Roads[/b] also extend influence.
[*] [b]Destroyed buildings[/b] reduce influence, meaning losing key structures can quickly cut off an important expansion.
[/list]

[h2]Building Requirements[/h2]
There are a variety of conditions required to construct a new Andarian building. 

[list]
[*] [b]Resource Costs[/b] - Buildings cost resources to produce, with the most common resources being gold, stone, wood, and iron.
[*] [b]Terrain and blocking[/b] - You must place a building in an unobstructed place within your sphere of influence.
[*] [b]Technological Unlocks[/b] - Some buildings require an architect to place, some require certain buildings, like a Lumber Yard or Blacksmith to construct properly.
[/list]

[h2]Step-by-Step Construction[/h2]
Building constructed by the Kingdom of Andar follow a multi-phase process:
https://youtu.be/sr1yABrZN7g

[list]
[*] [b]Foundation Laying[/b] – Workers clear terrain and mark the construction site.
[*] [b]Framework Setup[/b] – Wooden scaffolding is erected, defining the structure’s shape.
[*] [b]Assembly & Reinforcement[/b] – The building takes shape as walls, roofs, and details are finalized.
[*] [b]Completion & Functionality[/b] – Once fully built, the structure is operational and can train units, produce resources, or provide defensive bonuses.
[/list]

The time and resources required depend on the structure’s size and complexity. Upgraded buildings take longer but offer significant benefits.

[h2]Dynamic Destruction
[/h2]
War is brutal, and so is the destruction system in The Old War.

[list]
[*] [b]Progressive Damage[/b] – Instead of instantly vanishing, structures start to burn and crumble depending on the damage type.
[*] [b]Critical Damage[/b] – When a building gets critically damaged, it will be destroyed unless repaired.
[*] [b]Total Destruction[/b] – The building fully collapses and stops working. 
[/list]

These are the basics of the construction system for the Kingdom of Andar. Many of the same elements will be consistent across factions. 

Let me know if there is something you think could be added or changed!

notes.title: Unit Ability Improvements
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/a2e7877562fbe42c801a5b3433403f23e814b3a3.png[/img]

Battles are about to become more dynamic. Units now have a stamina system that adds another layer of strategy to movement and combat. With this update, positioning, timing, and stamina management will play an even greater role in securing victory. Whether it is repositioning your troops rapidly, or escaping a deadly ambush, being able to hustle troops out of there will save lives. When combined with knowing you can save your units to fight another day, this will make sure you keep their stamina in mind in a risky engagement.

[h2]New Unit Abilities[/h2]
[b]Stamina Bars[/b] – Most actions, such as sprinting and power attacks, will consume stamina. Managing stamina wisely will be crucial in prolonged engagements.

[b]Running[/b] – Units will no longer be forced to march at a slow pace. Sprinting will allow for faster movement across the battlefield but will drain stamina. This will allow you to move across terrain at a less leisurely pace if the need arises.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PWKNP8jrtGQ

[b]Power Attacks[/b] – The unit delivers stronger, more deliberate strikes that deals increased damage but costs stamina. Timing these attacks will be key to breaking enemy lines.

[b]Brace Shield[/b] – Defensive units can now brace against incoming attacks, reducing damage and holding their ground more effectively. Perfect for countering enemy charges.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3QdMQwv6guU

[b]Focus[/b] – With specific units & heroes, you can focus on them, giving you the ability to experience the game in a more visceral way.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wbiIzVcKGK8

These changes will create more fluid and tactical battles, rewarding players who adapt and use their units efficiently. 

Let us know what you think, and if you have any suggestions for additional abilities!

notes.title: Upgraded to the High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP)
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/fc2783ce0f425ddb8b7adc55b3a94a20502edfe4.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

It's been a while, but I have a number of very solid excuses so I hope you will forgive me.

I lost my job, got a new job, went to Scotland and got married. It's been a hell of a year. All that being said, I still do have some pretty solid updates for The Old War, and I can't wait to share them with you. 

First and foremost, I switched from using Unity's Universal Render Pipeline (URP) to the High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP). This was a tough choice for me, because I have always been that guy with a potato for a PC. I want people to be able to freely play this game with their friends regardless of their bank accounts. All that being said, the limitations on the number of lights were an unacceptable trade-off. 

Secondly, I switched from using Mirror to Netcode for GameObjects. I'm still unsure if this was the right call, but I really wanted to try out Netcode as it is being developed. Mirror also doesn't allow you to change the Enter Play Mode settings, which allows dramatically faster testing for the game.

The final major change is that I am no longer using Unity's NavMesh, I have switched to the A* Pathfinding Project. This is a brilliant library that eases a lot of the navigation issues I have been running into. 

Just about every change here was a major improvement to the Old War universe, so I hope you like it.

Dan
Warchest Studios

notes.title: Coming Soon Page Released!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42328726/3b9f3201be9132b01cb8983f47e7e15f09ab0d10.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

My name is Dan Marshall, and I am the indie developer behind The Old War. I am pleased to announce the release of my Coming Soon page and the Community Hub!

This is an exciting milestone for me, as I have been working on the development of The Old War for the past three years. It has evolved from a personal project into a full-blown RTS with multiplayer support.

This game stemmed out of a love for RTS and multiplayer games, and also from frustration that there weren't that many great co-op RTS games out there. I am the VP of Engineering at an AI-based startup, and I have numerous friends and colleagues helping with the project.

My vision  is for The Old War to become a deep and compelling game that you can play with your friends in many ways and have an equally deep and compelling endgame. The current slate of RTS games are rinse and repeat games with a single player campaign and multiplayer battles, and I find that they do not have the staying power I would like. I want to change all that by adding features from other games with excellent multiplayer and endgame support. I hope that by showing you can do new things and implement interesting features from other genres, you can really enhance the long term experience in RTS games. 

The final game will come with the following game modes to name a few:

[list]
[*] Co-op Campaign (With joint control as an Add-On later)
[*] Dungeons
[*] Sieges
[*] Bastions
[*] Daemon Portals
[/list]

It will also have these features to enhance the depth and gameplay:

[list]
[*] Commander (Player) Experience and Skill Trees
[*] Ancient Relics
[*] Persistent Armies
[*] Custom Races
[*] Unit Equipment
[*] Unit Levelling and Skill Trees
[*] Conquered Territory Bonuses
[/list]
There are many more features I want to implement, but to avoid just gushing about the project I will end it there! I hope you think this sounds interesting and fun, and I can't wait to chat with you about it!

Dan
